title: 2026 Bespoked Osaka Picks 01: Après, D3, Project D, Prova, Sour, Tailfin, Vigore – John Watson
content:
Maido from Osaka! Cari and John were in attendance at the 2026 Bespoked Osaka event, where they documented a variety of bikes from the global framebuilding community. Read on for a look at the Bespoked Osaka venue and a selection of builders including Après, D3, Project D, Prova, Sour/Tailfin, and Vigore…

Bespoked Osaka

For the first time, Bespoked, the largest handmade bike show in the world, landed in Japan, setting its eyes on the city of Osaka. This port city has a low-key vibe compared to Tokyo, with a vibrant cycling scene and reverence for craft, style, and functionality. For its venue, Bespoked chose the Glion Museum, which is home to classic and modern cars from around the globe.

This 10,000-square-meter property consists of four buildings, two of which were used to house the Bespoked showcase. It was built in 1923 originally as a port authority and features pre-war brick and timber construction. Bespoked settled into  two adjacent buildings the Thursday before the showcase and come Friday morning, it was bustling with builders and industry attendees.

On display was a mixture of classic road and touring bikes, built to the highest Japanese standards, to experimental designs from Europe, and just about everything in between. My intent with this showcase coverage was to pay homage to the builders of Japan, while still highlighting some of the global attendees. I hope you enjoy my Picks 01.

Velo Après Touring Bike

Velo Après makes classic-lined French-inspired touring and randonneuring bicycles. With two trim options available, the “Standard” comes nicely equipped with Shimano Claris for around $3,000 US, or the “Special” with a higher-end groupset and saddle for around $3,500. Those prices are for complete bikes.

Raijin Works makes these frames by hand, to the Velo Après specifications with ten colors to choose from, disc or rim configuration, and seven set sizes. Special add-ons are available, such as this stunning front randonneuring rack, rear racks, or other touring accouterments.

Japanese Kasai tubing is used to ensure the proper ride feel with a fork that planes and a frame that dances with you on your ride. Bang for buck, this bike is hard to beat.

@VeloAprès

D3 Lab Moridge Hardtail Cargo Bike

Beijing-based D3 Lab was the first bike at the 2026 Bespoked Osaka showcase that caught my eye. Ok, that’s an understatement. It blew me away. The two minds behind D3 Lab, Du and Joe, were putting the finishing touches on the bike as I was admiring the end-of-day golden-hour light at the Glion Museum. Still working out my photo setup, I wheeled the bike out into the expanse of the pre-war brick facility, looking for a quiet corner to poke and prod this creation with my lens.

This bricolage assemblage utilizes two distinct construction techniques, meshing traditional tubing brazing with laser-cut truss framing for the front platform’s structure. Inspired by triple triangle track bikes, the seat tube is kinked, and the seat stays dropped, allowing the wheel to be tucked in close towards the bottom bracket, making it incredibly nimble and maneuverable. The 120 mm travel shock keeps the front end impact resistant when carrying a load.

For steering, rather than using a push rod, the Moridge utilizes a cable steering mechanism, which allows for adjustment vis-à-vis barrel adjusters.

Its name, “Moridge,” is a combination of “Mobile Bridge,” as the front truss support is inspired by Arete Structures commonly used in bridge design. The frame is powder-coated, with the brown parts all Cerakote. The colors were selected by the bag maker, Cyclofowl. The bag maker also designed a comic for D3 Lab showcasing the brand’s origin story: a crashed alien ship, which is also depicted on the head tube badge.

Various components like the Redshift ShockStop post were stripped and Cerakoted, designed to pair with the D3 Labs stem and riser bar. Truss spandrel triangles are incorporated throughout the frame and bags.

Du and Joe, it was a pleasure to meet you. I’m so elated with how these photos came out, and it was a really special evening spent documenting your work.

@D3Lab

Project D Lustra Low Pro Track Bike

In Latin, Lustra translates to a summary of your skill set, and in Polish, it means mirrored. For Łódź, Poland-based Project D, a brainchild of engineer Dominik Dominiak, the word couldn’t be a better-suited label for his stunning low pro track bike. Full stop. This is the most stunning bicycle I have documented this year, and these photos are echelon-level for someone who has spent his life turning a camera to the work of framebuilders.

Dominik was inspired to begin building bikes by a red Cherubim bike, built by the master Shinichi Konno, he saw at a NAHBS event one year. So when Bespoked announced its Osaka showcase, he got to sketching a design. His intent was to create one continuous line from the fork to the top tube, which would then shift to the seat stays, chainstays, and bifurcate into the seat and downtube.

While the saddle-to-bar drop looks aggressive, it’s actually based on Dominik’s road bike fit, placing his hands in the same position as the drops on his bike. Utilizing bullhorns allows him to lower the top tube considerably, giving the appearance of an aggressive fit, even though it is very comfortable. Unfortunately, he didn’t have pedals with him to ride the bike…

The bike’s mastery lies in the execution of the bullhorn bars and the steering assembly, which rotates around a radius without interrupting the visual lines of the frame. All of the seams are concealed on the back of the head tube, leaving the front of the bike void of any bolts or interruptions.

It took seven layers of paint to give the Lustra its red glow. The seat tube’s teardrop profile creates a stark visual line at the rear, while side reflections minimize its visual heft, giving it the appearance of a sword’s edge, intended to slice through the air.

Yes, this is innovation and art, but it is a functional bicycle with operable parts and beautiful, jaw-dropping design notes everywhere. The track and fork ends are the most elegant I’ve seen, and the entire bicycle is what one ought to expect from shows like Bespoked. Meeting Dominik was a real pleasure. Documenting his work was a dream.

If you fancy the Lustra, it is for sale. Contact Dominik for inquiries. As a more personal note, it was a real joy to connect with Dominik and document his work to the best of my ability. You’re one talented human, friend.

@ProjectDBicycles

Prova Evoluto Road

Melbourne-based Prova Cycles is the collective effort between Mark and Kelly Hester, two siblings obsessed with creating the world’s finest titanium bicycles. Together with Dan Knives of Superbe Velo Service, a master wheel builder who also builds each Prova for its customers, and the talented painters at Velo Craft, Prova continuously evolves its modus operandi. Debuting at the 2026 Bespoked Osaka show is the latest evolutionary step in its road design, the Evoluto.

The Evoluto is Prova’s take on the ultimate modern metal bike. It takes the learning of the Integrale and Speciale road platforms and adds a unique headtube and bottom bracket design. Mark designs each model in CAD, paying attention to using spline lines to create a visual edge that ties the bike’s form from the head tube all the way to the dropouts.

Since a Prova is custom, the Evoluto can be designed to clear either 35 mm or 40 mm tires, and the bike can be fitted with either an Enve integrated carbon fork or the Prova titanium fork. Extra effort was put in place on this bike’s wheels, with Dan Knives polishing the DT 180 hubs, to which Mark then etched the logos back onto the surface.

Known for its simple paint designs and ombré fades, Prova’s first foray into graphics is present with this Evoluto, which displays circular box lining, inspired by Japanese fans. Velo Craft’s expertise is on full display here, with impeccable linework and masking. The clearcoat’s 2 mm edging ensures the classic Japanese-inspired design stays tack sharp for years to come.

Mark, it’s always a pleasure to document you and your team’s work. Kelly, we wish you were here. Mark looks lonely in this hardstyle pose without you!

@ProvaCycles

Sour x Tailfin

For the 2026 Bespoked Osaka show, Tailfin’s marketing director James Bracey worked with Dresden, Germany-based Sour Bicycles to create a one-of-a-kind finish for its Space Cake all-road bike. Inspired by cumulonimbus clouds, illuminated by an ombré fade at sunset, this paint job transitions from lavender to pink, from top to bottom.

The bike is accessorized with custom R&D Tailfin bags, which display the aluminum structures of each model. Bracey added that customers have requested these bags before, for ease of locating their packed items.

Tailfin’s R&D bags are always a showstopper, and when teaming up with Sour Bicycles, it’s a winning combination.

@SourBicycles @Tailfin

Vigore Kyoto Yuki’s Road Bike

Kyoto-based Vigore was founded in 1929 as a bicycle shop called Kataoka Bicycle Shokai. In 1968, Shiro Kataoka began building bikes under the Vigore banner at that shop. Now, Masato Kataoka and his daughter Yuki are the only bespoke framebuilders in Kyoto. On display at the 2026 Bespoked Osaka show was Yuki’s new road bike, a bike she built from start to finish.

Yuki learned to build five years ago from her father, and she’s been thinking of the perfect road bike ever since she first learned the art of lugged framebuilding. She designed this bike to fit shorter riders, maintaining clean proportions of larger-sized bikes, while relying on 650b wheels. The profile and silhouette is incredibly balanced, and the bike’s smooth pedaling demeanor is ensured thanks to the slightly higher bottom bracket.

Kyoto is surrounded by mountains, so Yuki wanted a bike that could use modern groupsets. It’s designed with UDH dropouts, so customers can select a full-mount Sram kit, or a 2x setup from Shimano. The bike uses disc brakes for comfortable braking down mountain passes and the elegant bend to the fork is a nod to traditional road bikes.

Yuki and her father embody the Japanese tradition of passing down knowledge from one generation to the next. Vigore’s passion and precision framebuilding were on full display at the 2026 Bespoked Showcase…

@VigoreKyoto
